title: Tech Note: Guide for Converting to 4Dv18 and Newer
author: Erick Lui, Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Unicode mode / object notation compatibility settings

historical_commentary.text: This conversion guide documents a real, one-time historical transition (32-bit to 64-bit-only, deprecation of PICT images and subtables) that is now complete industry-wide; any database still needing this guide today would be extremely old and would also need to additionally cross the Design-Mode-to-Project-Mode transition and multiple ORDA/4D Write Pro/View Pro migrations not covered here.
related_updates: 32-bit vs 64-bit conversion is now moot; all supported 4D versions are 64-bit only and this has been true for years
PICT image format and subtables were already legacy at the time of writing and are essentially nonexistent in databases still viable to convert
4D View classic / 4D Write classic referenced as needing rewriting are now fully superseded by 4D View Pro / 4D Write Pro
Databases converting today would follow a much longer path also including binary-to-Project-mode conversion, which this note does not cover
